acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.

This material was transferred to the RAC as part of five larger accessions between 2021 and 2023. These accessions were ingested by the RAC as Accessions 2021:067, 2021:108, 2021:134, 2022:019, and 2023:055.
The 2023:055 accession was originally given to the Ford Foundation by Nick Menzies with a 2020 certificate of gift.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains the office files of the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Field Office. It consists of three series.

The first series is comprised of a set of office files created by Nick Menizes who was Program Officer for Rural Poverty and Resources in the Beijing Office between 1990 and 1995. Menzies' files document the Beijing Office's development of its rural development and environment programming with specific focus on social forestry development in Yunnan.

The second series is made up of Beijing Office staff chronology files created between 1992 and 2004. These files contain outgoing correspondence created by Office staff with a diverse set of positions and program focuses including: Lisa Stearns, consultant for activities related to the United Nations 1995 World Conference on Women in Beijing; Stephen McGurk, Program Officer responsible for economics training and research; Andrew Watson, Foundation Representative for China; and Jonathan Hecht, Program Officer for human rights and governance.
The last series in the collection contains subject files created by the Beijing Office. These files concern Office programming and administration and intersect with the files in the first two series.

Programming areas engaged by the Beijing Office that are documented throughout the whole of the collection include women and gender, reproductive health, family planning and population, economic development, poverty reduction, rural development, environment, internal migration and the shift from urban to rural environments in China, human rights, law, public policy, civil society, China-U.S. relations, and culture.

In addition to those already described, common material formats found throughout the collection include memos, drafts, notebooks, notes, reports, grant-related documents, articles, meeting materials, press releases, press clips, and publications. There are also some photographs, digital media, and a VHS tape.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Ford Foundation established its field office in Beijing, China in 1988. Prior to opening that office, the Foundation managed to directly engage the country for several years through collaborating with the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) to make grants. This work began in 1979 after China and the United States established diplomatic relations. CASS then helped the Foundation to negotiate the establishment of an office in China and was made the Foundation's host when the office was approved. Within the Foundation, the Beijing Office was situated within its larger Asia Programs.

Throughout its history, the Ford Foundation's Beijing Office has engaged in a number of different program areas including economics, legal reform, China-U.S. relations and other international relations work, public policy, environment and development, the impact of China's global development, poverty reduction, the social impact of urbanization, education, women, reproductive health, and civil society.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The collection was originally processed as Ford Foundation records, Beijing Office, Nick Menzies files. When additional records from the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Field Office was transferred to the Rockefeller Archive Center, the Menzies files were absorbed into a larger Ford Foundation records, Beijing Field Office Files collection.

did.physdesc: The bindings on some of the field notebooks have started to deteriorate. Notebooks should be handled carefully.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series differs from the others in the collection because the records it contains were gifted from Nick Menizes to the Ford Foundation and then later transferred to the Rockefeller Archive Center. The series contains the office files Menzies created and maintained when he worked as Program Officer for Rural Poverty and Resources in the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Office between 1990 and 1995. There are also earlier materials from when Menzies worked for Winrock International in China between 1988 and 1989 and some later digital media Menzies added when he gifted the records to the Foundation in 2020. Through these different groups of records, the series documents the development of the Foundation's Rural Poverty and Resources Program in China from the time the Beijing Office opened in 1988 to when Menzies left China in 1995. The materials especially highlight the Foundation's support for social forestry management in the Yunnan province of China.

There are three main parts of the series. The first part includes Menzies' gift of certificate for the records, contents description of the records, and digital media. The certificate contextualizes Menzies' work in the Beijing Office and explains how the materials were transferred to the Foundation. Researchers can use the certificate and the file-level contents description on the inventory to gain a stronger understanding of the other materials in the series. There is a description of the file directory of the digital media item. The files on this item include maps, program reviews, field visit reports, presentations, and grant related documents. Additionally, it contains a 2016 article.

The next part of the series comprises a set of field notebooks Menzies used when he worked in China between 1988 and 1995. The notebooks span across both his positions at Winrock International and the Ford Foundation. They document program field visits throughout various counties in the Yunnan province and other locations in China. Some of these visits were to grantees and potential grantees. A few other items are interspersed throughout the notebooks. They include maps, loose notes, correspondence, and business cards.
The last part of the series contains a group of appointment calendars Menzies used while working in China.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Records in this series come from Accession 2023:055 which was originally given to the Ford Foundation by Nick Menzies in a 2020 certificate of gift. It was later transferred to the RAC in 2023.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series is comprised of chronology files created by staff members of the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Field Office. Chronology files contain the outgoing correspondence of the staff members and are organized by date. Some files are further organized alphabetically by correspondent.
The series includes chronology files created by Lisa Stearns, Stephen McGurk, Andrew Watson, and Jonathan Hecht.

Lisa Stearns worked as a consultant for the Foundation and focused on activities related to the 1995 Fourth World Conference on Women in Beijing. Her correspondence extends from 1993 to 1995 and concerns preparation for the conference, supporting participants to attend the conference, communications and media strategy, and meetings ahead of the conference.

Stephen McGurk was a Program Officer at the Beijing Office and was responsible for the Foundation's economics training and research program in China. His correspondence in the series runs from 1993 to 1999 and concerns economic development and reform, the socio-economic transformation from rural to urban environments in China, and poverty reduction.

Andrew Watson served as the Beijing Office's Representative for China. His correspondence extends from when he was appointed as Representative in 1999 to 2004. In addition to discussing a range of program interests like economic development, public policy, civil society, gender, arts and culture, and China-U.S. relations, his correspondence also discusses Office administration and policies.

Jonathan Hecht was a Program Officer for human rights and governance in the Beijing Office. The correspondence in his chronological file reflects this program focus. There are a few pieces of correspondence in his file that were created by Phyllis Chang who succeeded Hecht in his position at the Beijing Office.

physdesc.extent: 28 document boxes: 23 letter boxes and 5 legal boxes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains subject files created and maintained by the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Field Office. The files concern the Office's programming and administration and originate from between the Office's opening in 1988 and the mid-2000s with the bulk of the materials having been created in the 1990s.

A large amount of the files in the series document the Ford Foundation's preparations for the United Nations 1995 Fourth World Conference on Women in Beijing in relation to Foundation-Administered Project (FAP) 09390007. They highlight the work of Foundation consultant Lisa Stearns whose chronology files are contained in Series 2 of the collection. The Beijing Office's broader support for women, reproductive health, and gender issues are documented throughout the files.

Other program areas the subject files highlight include civil society in China and broader Asia, economic development, poverty reduction, rural development, education, law, and internal migration within China.
The files also document program strategy development across the Foundation's Asia region programs in the 1990s and foundation-wide program strategy transitions.

In addition to the connections researchers can discover between the subject files in this series and Lisa Stearns chronology files in Series 2, there are also links to other staff chron files in Series 2 and Nick Menzies' office files in Series 1.

did.physdesc: File contains still images. Images are 31 photo contact sheets.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The photo contact sheets contain images created by photographer Rhodri Jones who the Ford Foundation hired to take photographs of its China Office grantees in 1997. The Foundation later consulted these sheets when searching for grantees still active in 1999 for inclusion in its annual report for that year. There are separate descriptions and notes created by Jones for the images.

The grantees documented in the images include a migrants' school, a women's legal advice service, the Yixian Micro Finance Project, and the Zhejiang Village Migrant Community Project. There are images of Beijing and portraits of people.
